item.title: Gelato 0.5.1
item.description:
Gelato 0.5.1 (beta)

0.5 went out as a regular release by mistake. 0.5.1 is the beta it should have been, plus one small change.

  • Settings › Updates shows “· beta”, and feedback reports the beta channel.
  • Rig checks are off again, as in earlier betas.
  • The welcome window’s gel strip is now 3 pt.
  • If you installed 0.5, turn on “Get beta updates” to keep getting betas.

item.title: Gelato 0.5
item.description:
Gelato 0.5 (beta)

A page for each show, a fuller colour page, and an anonymous daily check-in you can turn off.

  • Shows: open a show to browse its lights and colours, and delete a colour or a light from that show alone.
  • A colour’s page has its name as a big title, fills the window’s width, and keeps the window’s minimum size.
  • For a family of lights, a colour’s page names the light the colour comes from and the lights that follow it.
  • Choose a version right in the To Choose list.
  • A gel the catalogue knows only by its maker’s name shows that name beside the code.
  • On the import’s Palettes step, groups with nothing ticked start closed.
  • The main window’s gel strip is thinner and clears the toolbar.
  • Settings ▸ Updates ▸ Privacy: Gelato sends an anonymous check-in once a day, so we can count installs. It sends a random id made on your Mac, Gelato’s and macOS’s versions, the kind of Mac and the kind of licence: nothing about you, your shows or your library. The id is kept only as a code that changes every day, so one Mac can’t be followed from day to day, and check-ins are deleted after 90 days. Your IP address is used only to limit how often a Mac can check in, and isn’t kept. Turn it off and nothing is sent.

item.title: Gelato 0.4
item.description:
Gelato 0.4 (beta)

Faster imports, multicell lights matched by their colour, and a gel strip in the main window.

  • Importing a large export is much faster, and the progress bar covers the whole wait, including after Import on the Palettes step.
  • On the Palettes step, tick or untick a whole section with its header’s box.
  • The import’s counts no longer jitter as they change.
  • Lights are matched by the colour parameters they have, so a multicell light’s cells can share a single light’s colours. You can also link a single light to any cell yourself.
  • A Parameters section shows which colour parameters two lights share, and which only one has.
  • The main window has a gel strip along the top, and a colour’s page takes its own colour for the strip and a soft glow.
  • The welcome window’s gel strip is taller and stays whole on macOS 15.

item.title: Gelato 0.3
item.description:
Gelato beta

Thanks for trying the first beta. Everything below works with your tester licence.

What’s in it

  • Import a CSV export of an Eos show file. Colour palettes are filed by gel and by light; any it can’t read a gel from wait in To Match.
  • See the versions of a mix side by side, and choose the one builds use.
  • Build a new show’s palettes in Blind after one confirmation, or export the build as a CSV to import yourself.
  • Add a colour in tech (L602, say), from the app or from a Stream Deck through Companion.
  • Preview a colour on a light from your own command line. Nothing is recorded.
  • Turn on the show-mode lock and nothing is written to the console.
  • Updates: with Settings ▸ Updates ▸ Get beta updates on, each new beta arrives here. Nothing installs while a console is connected.

Not in it yet

  • Buying Gelato. Your tester licence is free for three months.
  • The Companion module in Bitfocus’s list. Ask us for it at the address below.

Feedback

Choose Help ▸ Send Feedback…. It opens an email with your version and any recent crash reports attached. Or write to support@flatfield.co.

Libraries you make from this beta on keep working in every later build.

item.title: Gelato 0.2
item.description:
Gelato 0.2 (beta)

A new look for the welcome window and the installer, and clearer licences.

  • The welcome window has a new look, with a gel strip along the top.
  • The installer opens on a designed window: drag Gelato to Applications.
  • Adding a licence shows a tick and a line saying it was added. A key this version doesn’t accept says so on its own line.
  • A Gelato Pro licence now says Pro.
  • After an import, the banner counts the palettes taken from the rig.
  • On the import’s steps, a long show name takes a second line before it’s shortened.
  • Families’ toolbar buttons drop their labels only when the window is too narrow for them.
  • Versions are now numbered 0.2, 0.3 and so on.
